Greptile Summary

This PR fixes debounced disk-state persistence so repeated writes for the same token retain the latest state while preserving the original flush schedule. - Replaces the state in an existing frozen `QueueItem` using `dataclasses.replace`. - Adds regression coverage confirming both the queued and persisted values reflect the latest `set_state` call.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains.

Import

The implementation looks correct to me. Replacing the queued `QueueItem` state while preserving the original timestamp
  fixes the stale flush without changing debounce timing.

  One CI issue remains: pyright flags the test because it assigns through `state_manager.__dict__`. Replacing those two
  assignments with `object.__setattr__(..., "states_directory", tmp_path)` fixes the type error locally.

Thanks for the thorough review, really appreciate it.

On the pyright issue you're right, reaching into __dict__ was the wrong move even though it happened to work at runtime (since states_directory is a cached_property and that's basically how it stores its value anyway). object.__setattr__ is more explicit about what's actually happening and it's a pattern pyright understands. Swapped both occurrences and reran the disk state manager tests locally — all still passing.
